subject.title: resolveCliAuthEpoch invalidates every live CLI session when local credential source-of-storage flips, even though identity is unchanged

question: What Claude CLI identity signal should reusable-session auth epochs trust when OpenClaw has both an auth-profile credential and a local Claude credential source whose storage presence can appear or disappear?
rationale: Current code can reset live sessions for storage-shape churn, but relaxing the epoch without an accepted identity boundary could preserve a session across a real or unprovable account change.

options.title: Narrow Identity-Stable Fix
options.body: Use a Claude CLI-specific internal fix that ignores storage-presence churn only when the unchanged identity boundary is proven, and fail closed for logout or unproven account changes.

options.title: Accept Host Credential Ownership
options.body: Allow the local Claude credential to own the epoch for Claude CLI sessions and document the security tradeoff around the available host identity signal.

options.title: Keep Fail-Closed Behavior
options.body: Leave the current invalidation behavior in place and document user-side mitigation for setups with credential source churn.

recommendation.title: Narrow Identity-Stable Fix
recommendation.body: Use a Claude CLI-specific internal fix that ignores storage-presence churn only when the unchanged identity boundary is proven, and fail closed for logout or unproven account changes.

likelyOwner.reason: Josh already gave item-specific guidance on the overlapping PR about avoiding a public host-only mode and preserving resets for changed or unproven auth identity.
